head_commit.message:
[XLA] Enforce page_size_kib in BufferAssignment::CombineTempAllocations

When `page_size_kib > 0`, `AssignBuffersFromHeapSimulator` partitions sequential
temporary buffers into pages of at most `page_size_kib * 1024` bytes. Standalone
temporary allocations created outside the heap simulator, such as temporary
tuples or buffers with custom interference, default to `page_id = 0`.
`CombineTempAllocations` previously merged them against
`multiheap_size_constraint_per_heap_`, allowing page 0 to exceed the page limit.

Order heap simulator pages ahead of standalone `Color(0)` allocations and pack
overflow buffers into existing `Color(0)` pages with enough aligned tail space.
Assign a fresh unique `page_id` whenever no existing page fits or a fixed offset
prevents merging. Behavior when `page_size_kib == 0` is unchanged.

Tests:
- `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/service:buffer_assignment_test`: pins
  page tail packing, new page creation and reuse, and fixed offset uniqueness.

display_title: [XLA] Check combined window in pad ReduceWindow broadcast rewrite

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check combined window in pad ReduceWindow broadcast rewrite

When `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleReduceWindow` folds a `kPad` into a
`kReduceWindow`, `is_effective_broadcast` replaces the pair with a broadcast of
the unpadded operand. The check previously inspected only the `kPad`
configuration and ignored existing padding and window dilation on the
`kReduceWindow` itself. When the `kReduceWindow` carried window padding, output
windows covering only padding elements were rewritten to the operand value, and
padding on dimensions larger than 1 crashed `CreateBroadcastSequence`.

Compute the combined `Window` first and check `is_effective_broadcast` against
static shapes, requiring trivial windows on dimensions not equal to 1 and full
endpoint window coverage without cropping or window dilation on size 1
dimensions. If the combined window is not a broadcast, also check whether the
`kReduceWindow` alone is already an effective broadcast of its operand and
replace it without folding the `kPad`.

head_commit.message:
Flatten WeightedPicker tree into a single heap array.

`WeightedPicker` allocated `num_levels_` separate heap arrays (`new int32*[num_levels_]` plus one array per tree level), incurring `num_levels_ + 1` allocations and deallocations on construction, destruction, and resize while pointer-chasing across levels on every `PickAt` and `set_weight` call.

Store all internal nodes and leaves in a single 1-indexed binary heap array of size `1 << num_levels_`, eliminating per-level pointer indirection and cutting tree allocation to a single block.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Skip implicit broadcast rewrite for zero-bound dynamic dims

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix out-of-bounds slice in DynamicPadder implicit broadcast rewrite

RewriteDynamicBinaryOp inserts an implicit broadcast when the operands of an
elementwise binary op have a dynamic dimension with different runtime sizes.
The rewrite extracts a size-1 slice along the dimension, reshapes the
dimension away and broadcasts the result back to the full shape.

When the dimension's static bound is zero the dimension is always empty: both
dynamic sizes are necessarily zero, so no implicit broadcast can ever be
needed. The rewrite nevertheless ran and emitted an out-of-bounds slice,

  slice(%a), slice={[0:1], [0:2]}   // %a: f32[0,2]

which fails HLO verification with

  limit index (1) must be less than or equal to dimension size (0)

This is reachable from TF through tf.math.is_non_decreasing and
tf.math.is_strictly_increasing, which wrap the comparison in a tf.cond whose
branch operands end up with a zero bound:
https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/49925

Skip the rewrite when the static bound of the dimension is zero and add a
regression test.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Emit parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce lowering

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Emit parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce lowering

Reducers like `(a, b) -> b`, which JAX emits for "take last" regions, contain
no instruction to emit: their result is one of the reducer block arguments.
EmitReduceComputation assumed otherwise and failed with `!to_emit.empty()` as
soon as such a reduce ended up in a Triton normalization fusion.

That alone was not enough. CombineReduceResultsWithInitValues maps the reducer
arguments in reverse order, which is invisible for commutative combiners but
makes the post-combine return the init value for `(a, b) -> b`. Map the
accumulator to the init value and the element to the tt.reduce result.

Add a deviceless lit test that runs the fusion through fusion_to_triton, and
fix the expectation of @reduce_with_multiple_inputs, whose reducer only kept a
live tt.reduce thanks to the reversed mapping.

display_title: [XLA] Reanalyze changed computations incrementally in HloRematerialization

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reanalyze changed computations incrementally in HloRematerialization

`HloRematerialization` runs `HloDataflowAnalysis` with `ssa_form=false`,
`propagate_through_calls=false`, and `propagate_through_control_flow=false`.
Previously, each peak priority rematerialization step discarded the entire
analysis and reran `HloDataflowAnalysis::Run` across every computation in the
module.

Add `HloDataflowAnalysis::ReanalyzeComputation` to update only a mutated
computation and any newly cloned callees in a single post order pass. Track
stale computations in `HloRematerialization` so unchanged computations are not
reanalyzed. No generated HLO behavior changes.

`BM_PeakPriorityRematMultiComputation` median CPU time (16 rematerializations):

| Fusions | Before | After | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | 14.88 ms | 6.68 ms | 2.23x |
| 64 | 54.31 ms | 13.25 ms | 4.10x |
| 256 | 239.25 ms | 46.14 ms | 5.18x |

Tests:
- `hlo_dataflow_analysis_test`: pins `ReanalyzeComputation` equivalence.
- `hlo_rematerialization_test`: pins nested fusion rematerialization and
  adds `BM_PeakPriorityRematMultiComputation`.

head_commit.message:
Batch output buffer allocations per memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

Dispatching executables with many outputs currently invokes `AllocateRawBufferForExecute` and constructs a debug-annotation closure once per non-aliased output leaf, while `ExecuteOptions::use_output_arena` couples all output buffer lifetimes to the longest-lived output.

Add `PjRtRawClient::AllocateRawBuffersForExecute` (defaulting to a loop over `AllocateRawBufferForExecute` so existing backends preserve their behavior) and group non-aliased output allocations by memory space in `CommonPjRtClient::AllocateOutputBuffersWithInputReuse` so backends can allocate decoupled output buffers in a single batch per memory space.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Add IfrtDcePass to eliminate dead IFRT ops and unused outputs

Add `IfrtDcePass` (`-ifrt-dce`) to walk IFRT functions in reverse order and:
1. Erase unused outputs (or the entire op when all array outputs and `control_output` are unused) from `ifrt.Reshard`, `ifrt.BitcastArrays`, `ifrt.CopyArrays` ops, and from `ifrt.RemapArrays` ops (pruning unreferenced `ifrt.RemapArrays` inputs and compacting `in_array_index` and `out_array_index` in kept `IfrtArrayMappingAttr` entries).
2. Erase unused `ifrt.Call` results and corresponding callee `func.return` operands, simplify callee regions, erase unused callee block arguments and `ifrt.Call` inputs (remapping `io_aliases`, `donated_input_indices`, `arg_attrs`, and `res_attrs`), and erase dead empty `ifrt.Call` ops along with unused private callees.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Register F16 conversion libcalls on PowerPC

head_commit.message:
Register F16 conversion libcalls on PowerPC

#ai-generated

LLVM lowers F16 <-> F32 conversions on PowerPC to calls to
__extendhfsf2 and __truncsfhf2, but the XLA:CPU JIT defines them only
on Apple and s390x, so every F16 computation on a PowerPC host fails
with

  Symbols not found: [ __extendhfsf2, __truncsfhf2 ]

Map them to XLA's own __gnu_h2f_ieee and __gnu_f2h_ieee. Those take and
return F16 values as uint16_t on PowerPC, as the libcalls do, so no
runtime library has to provide these symbols.
